findings.evidence: "The ~436 GB KV budget (640 − 140 − 64, §5.3(b)) supports ~436/24.9 ≈ 17.5, i.e. 17 whole-slot concurrent 9,500-token requests per host ... against the initial 9.2K KV alone the quotient is ≈18 (436 ÷ 24.1), matching Ch 4 §4.6."
findings.issue: The text says "supports ~436/24.9 ≈ 17.5, i.e. 17 whole-slot" but does not explicitly state that the 17 is a floor and that the input-only 18 is not used for fleet sizing. The distinction is stated elsewhere, but this occurrence can be read as two competing concurrency ceilings.
findings.fix_instruction: Add "floored to 17; the input-only quotient of 18 is shown only for reconciliation and is not the slot-counting basis" after the first quotient.

findings.page: PDF p.123 (printed p.99); supporting text PDF p.121 (printed p.97) and PDF p.124 (printed p.100)
findings.evidence: Table 5-2 rows (PDF p.123): "Selection status | recommended, pending target-corpus validation | [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]" and "Verdict | Embedding: all-mpnet-base-v2 (768-dim); Generation: 70B FP16 on 8×H100 | Selection surfaces (§5.1) [canonical scenario][DERIVED]". But §5.3(a) (PDF p.121) states the quality basis of that verdict: "Assume, as a scenario input rather than a measured result, a quality-vs-dimension uplift of up to ~15% MAP [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] (a chosen input, not a cited finding — no study is invoked here)", and the same section hedges the recommendation ("the quality claim itself is the §5.3(a)/§5.7 item still to validate on the target corpus"). The chapter's own rule (PDF p.124, Table 5-2 note): "The mixed-input convention therefore governs: the non-canonical input wins, and the rows carry [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] rather than [canonical scenario][DERIVED]".
findings.issue: Provenance/label mismatch: the Table 5-2 verdict and selection-status rows carry [canonical scenario] provenance even though the embedding-model recommendation's decisive input is explicitly an [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] (~15% MAP uplift) whose transfer to the target corpus is an open [HYPOTHESIS]. Under the chapter's own stated mixed-input convention (non-canonical input wins → [ILLUSTRATIVE]), these two rows are mislabeled. The error matters because the two provenance tags are the book's mechanism for telling a reader which numbers survive re-derivation against a real corpus and a procured quote.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the Table 5-2 "Selection status" and "Verdict" rows to [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] / [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] respectively (or split the row so the generation-model verdict keeps [canonical scenario][DERIVED] while the embedding-model verdict carries [ILLUSTRATIVE]), and add the same mixed-input note that the per-dollar rows already carry.
